compare.heading: Statements written in Lean
compare.intro: Lean is a language for mathematical statements and proofs that a computer can verify. Here each Lean statement appears beside a possible paper counterpart. The note between them explains why they were linked.
compare.supporting_heading: What the release’s Lean states, and the theorem it is paired with
compare.index_intro: Choose one to see it beside the paper theorem it is paired with.

state_head.producer-declared-binding: The Lean statement OpenAI links to this theorem

state_qual.candidate-pairing: Selected from shared wording. No review of whether the statements mean the same thing is recorded.
state_qual.producer-cited-association: The Lean source cites this theorem. No review of whether the statements mean the same thing is recorded.
state_qual.producer-declared-binding: OpenAI explicitly links these statements. No review of whether they mean the same thing is recorded.
state_qual.unavailable: No paper theorem is paired with it.

compare.no_pair: No paper theorem is paired with this Lean statement.
compare.paired_many: It is paired with {labels}, each shown below.

compare.lean_support: the release lists it as a supporting statement
compare.lean_more_one: The file states one more theorem:

compare.holes_many: {n} definitions are compared by name and type only: {names}.
compare.nolean: The release has no Lean statement for this family. Its papers remain available to read, and contributors can propose a formal statement of a result.
compare.sorry: This file states the theorem with sorry, a placeholder, in place of its proof. OpenAI supplies a separate proof file. Comparator tests whether that proof proves the statement here.
compare.heading_one: One selected Lean statement for checking
compare.source_notes_heading: Lean source and the scope of the reports
compare.intro_one: Lean is a language for mathematical statements and proofs that a computer can verify. The Lean statement below is shown beside its possible paper counterpart, with the reason they were linked.
compare.row_candidate: Possible Lean counterpart of {label} in {paper}, found from shared wording; not reviewed.
compare.row_cited: Its source cites {label} in {paper}; the match is not reviewed.
compare.row_declared: OpenAI links it to {label} in {paper}; no review of whether the statements mean the same thing is recorded.
compare.row_none: No paper theorem is paired with it.
compare.comparator_once: For a configured theorem, the [[comparator|Comparator]] program tests whether OpenAI’s separate proof proves the exact Lean statement using only the allowed axioms. Some [[challenge|statement files]] instead configure definitions for comparison by name and type. Acceptance does not establish that a formal statement means the same thing as the paper’s theorem.

readings.heading: Does the Lean express the advertised result?
readings.intro: {names} independently assessed whether this family’s Lean statements express the whole result OpenAI describes in its catalogue. These are assessments of the family as a whole, not of each paper theorem separately.

state.all: the Lean statements express or imply the whole advertised result
state.part: the Lean statements express part of the advertised result
state.narrower: the Lean statements express a narrower statement than the advertised result
state.weaker: the Lean statements express a weaker statement than the advertised result
state.supporting: the Lean statements express a supporting result
state.different: the Lean statements express a different result

readings.defs: Definitions the group asks readers to compare with the paper
readings.draft_heading: AI-drafted comparisons, with no recorded human review
readings.draft_fold: {n} AI-drafted comparisons, with no recorded human review

readings.producer_more: Read the rest of OpenAI’s note
readings.nolean: The release contains no Lean statement for this family, so there is no formal statement to compare with OpenAI’s description.

reruns.heading: Who ran the proof-verification program?
reruns.intro: These groups report running Comparator with the release’s Lean statement files. For a configured theorem, it verifies OpenAI’s separate proof against the exact statement; some files instead configure definitions for comparison by name and type. Each row is the named group’s report. Atlas has not repeated the runs.
reruns.none: Atlas has no report of an independent group running Comparator for this Lean statement.
reruns.receipt_label: Original report of {who} Comparator run for {name}
reruns.common_pin_one: One report, at the release’s recorded version.
reruns.common_pin_many: {n} reports, all at the release’s recorded version.
reruns.common_many: {n} reports, each at the version its row gives.
reruns.details_none: These reports do not list the software versions, proof-verification programs, axioms, time or memory in separate fields. Any such details in a report’s prose are reproduced below.
reruns.more: Re-runs of the other {n} Lean statements
reruns.others_intro: Other people’s accounts of running proof-verification software, with links to their reports.

method.hol_checks: Proof of a selected step in HOL Light

checks.intro: These reports examine claims in the papers using {kinds}, independently of the release’s Lean proofs. Read each report for the exact claim it covers.
checks.intro_none: These reports examine claims in the papers using methods other than the release’s Lean proofs. Read each report for the exact claim it covers.

intro_kind.hol_checks: HOL Light, a different proof assistant

checks.findings_intro: The program that collects Atlas’s source records, Statement Map, could not obtain or interpret some source material. These notes describe those limits; they do not identify mathematical errors.

left.heading: Questions awaiting review
left.reader_note_ref: its request is printed in full under {link}.
left.intro: Each item identifies a statement, definition or report that needs further review. Its link opens a GitHub form with the source version already recorded.

kinds.scope-review: Read the Lean statement against the paper
kinds.pairing-review: Compare the proposed paper and Lean matches
kinds.claim-identification: Identify the theorem the catalogue describes
kinds.reader-request: Address a question raised in an independent assessment
kinds.definition-review: Read the definitions the solution supplies
kinds.independent-check-followup: Investigate a calculation that did not decide the claim

left.check_each: Compare one Lean statement with its paper:

reasons.Lexical navigation candidate; catalogue: The theorem shown was selected from shared wording with OpenAI’s description. Atlas records no review confirming that it is the theorem the description means.
reasons.No unique candidate with at least three: No single paper statement clearly matches OpenAI’s description by wording, and no review identifying the intended theorem is recorded.
reasons.Read the solution-supplied definitions a: OpenAI’s proof file supplies some definitions. Atlas records no comparison confirming that they mean the same objects as the paper’s definitions.
reasons.No Lean object is recorded for this fami: The release has no Lean statement for this family.
reasons.The attributed exact check is undecided: An independent calculation did not decide the claim, or needs data absent from its source.
reasons.Recorded candidate or producer-declared: Atlas records no review of whether each linked Lean statement and paper theorem mean the same thing.
reasons.No imported accepted Comparator report b: Atlas records no independent report that Comparator accepted the proof at the release version shown here.
reasons.An AI scope draft has no named human rev: An AI agent drafted an assessment of which part of the paper this Lean statement expresses. No named human review is recorded.

left.reason_fallback: No completed review of this item is recorded.
